transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I feel a little silly even taking up your time, to be honest. I'm sure you see people with much bigger problems. But I came in because I just keep getting these... well, these really awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. 

I work with data, and my mind will just suddenly convince me I've put a wrong number in a data release, or... or even just everyday things, like leaving the back door unlocked, or paying a bill from the wrong account. And the really embarrassing part is, even when I absolutely know I checked it, my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some sort of huge disaster. I try to be rational about it, I really do, but I just can't seem to shake the feeling. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right... is that the sort of thing you help people with?
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking doors or rechecking your work, to try and get rid of these unwanted thoughts?

Well, um... I guess I do, a little bit. I mean, it's probably normal to double-check things, right? Everyone wants to be thorough. But, um... maybe I do it a bit more than most people. 

When I get those thoughts, I... well, to calm myself down, I might just reopen a spreadsheet real quick to make sure. Or, you know, I'll reread an email line by line before I send it. Just to be absolutely certain. And with the house, I'll check the locks, or look at my payment confirmations... but I kind of have to do it in a specific order. If I don't do it in that exact order, it just doesn't feel... safe, I guess? 

I know it sounds a bit much, and I try not to let it get out of hand. But, honestly, there are some nights where I'm still sitting at my desk hours after everyone else has logged off, just... going over things. And I haven't even really finished anything new. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely unhinged. Is it... is it okay that I do that? I mean, I'm just trying to be careful, but I know it's probably not the best way to handle it.
How much distress do these unwanted thoughts cause you on a daily basis?

Well, um... distress is a strong word, isn't it? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything. Lots of people have stressful jobs, and I know I'm lucky to have mine. 

But, I guess... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... it does get a little overwhelming sometimes. Actually, quite a bit overwhelming. The thoughts are just so loud, you know? And they don't really stop. 

I try to keep a smile on and push through it, because I don't want to be a burden or let anyone down. But there are days when the worry just sort of... consumes me. It feels like I'm constantly carrying this heavy weight, just waiting for the other shoe to drop. It takes up so much energy. 

I'm sorry, I'm probably making it sound worse than it is. I just... I really want to do a good job and be responsible. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting.
Do you feel like checking things in a specific order or repeating certain actions helps to reduce your anxiety about making mistakes?

Well, yes... I suppose it does help, at least for a little while. I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm doing all this just to be difficult or obsessive. I'm just trying to be a good employee, you know? 

But... yes, to calm myself down, I do end up reopening those spreadsheets. And I'll reread the emails, line by line, just to be sure. And with the house, it's the locks and the payment confirmations... I just check them over and over, and it has to be in that set order. If I do it right, it finally feels 'safe.' 

I know I mentioned earlier that it takes up some time, and... well, to be completely transparent—and I hope you won't judge me too harshly for this—some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and I haven't actually finished anything new. I just keep checking. 

It sounds so silly when I say it out loud. I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise. Is that... is that something you've seen before? I just hope I'm not the only one who does this.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking actions or they would not feel complete?

Well, yes... I think "complete" is exactly the right word for it. You know, like I was just saying with the, um, the spreadsheets and the emails? If I don't go through them line by line, or if I don't check the locks and the payment confirmations in that exact sequence... it just feels like something is terribly unfinished. 

I really have to do it over and over until it finally clicks and feels "safe." I know I just mentioned being stuck at my desk for hours without actually finishing anything new, and I'm so sorry to repeat myself! I just... I want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking? I really hope I'm being helpful and not just talking in circles. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel like there's something inherently 'right' or 'correct' about doing these checks in a specific order, beyond just making sure everything is accurate?

Well, um... I guess so? I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm, you know, overly particular or demanding. I know how annoying that can be for people. But... yes, there is a certain way it has to be done. 

Like I was saying before, with the spreadsheets and the emails... and the locks and the payment confirmations... it's not just about accuracy, I suppose. It's... well, if I don't do it in that exact set order, the feeling of it being 'safe' just never comes. It's like a puzzle piece that won't fit right unless you turn it exactly the correct way. 

And, um, I know I've brought this up already, and I'm so sorry if I'm dwelling on it, but that's why I end up sitting there for hours, reopening things over and over, not finishing anything new. I just... I have to keep going until that 'right' feeling hits. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too strange. I really am trying to just be thorough and responsible. Is it normal to feel like that?
Do you feel like the specific order in which you do these checks has to be symmetrical or exact in some way?

Well, um... symmetrical? I don't know if I'd use that exact word, but... yes, it definitely has to be exact. I really hope I'm not coming across as too rigid or, you know, difficult. I just... I want to do things properly.

But, yes, like I mentioned with the spreadsheets and the emails, and the locks... I have to do them in that exact set order. If I check the front door lock, I have to check the back door lock next, and then the payment confirmations in a very specific sequence. If I mess up the order, or if I get interrupted, I have to start the whole sequence over again. 

That's... that's why I end up reopening those spreadsheets and rereading the emails line by line, over and over, sometimes for hours, until it finally feels 'safe.' It's just so hard to stop until it's perfectly exact. 

I know I've said that a few times now, about being stuck at my desk with nothing actually finished, and I'm so sorry to keep repeating myself! I just... I want to make sure I'm answering your question about it being exact. Am I explaining that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like the exact order of your checking actions is what makes them feel complete, or is it something more about the actions themselves?

Well, um... I think it's both, honestly. I hope that's an okay answer. I really don't want to make things complicated for you.

It's the actions themselves, because doing them... it's the only thing that calms me down when I get that awful, anxious feeling. But it's also the exact order, because if I don't do it right, it doesn't work. 

Like I was saying, I end up reopening the spreadsheets, and rereading the emails line by line, and checking the locks and the payment confirmations over and over... and it has to be in that set order until it finally feels 'safe.' If I just did the actions randomly, it wouldn't help at all. 

That's why some nights I'm still sitting at my desk hours later, having accomplished absolutely nothing new. I just... I have to keep doing those specific actions, in that specific sequence, to calm myself down. 

I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, bringing up the spreadsheets and the desk again. I'm really sorry if I'm being repetitive or tedious! I just want to make sure I'm answering your question about whether it's the order or the actions. Did that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family, friends, or coworkers due to these thoughts and checking behaviors?

Well, um... I guess it has caused a few little hiccups here and there. Nothing too terrible, I hope! I really try my best not to let it affect anyone else, because I know how frustrating it must be for them. I hate being a burden. 

But, um... at work, I have fallen behind on some major deadlines. It's just that I stay so late trying to review everything—like the spreadsheets and the payment confirmations—and I still don't actually finish what I'm supposed to be doing. I just want everything to be perfect for my coworkers, you know? But I think they're starting to get a bit frustrated with me. 

And, socially... well, I haven't been going out much lately. I used to love going to salsa nights, and I'd go kayaking on the weekends with friends, but... I've stopped going. I just can't seem to get away from the checking and reviewing in time to meet up with them. By the time I feel 'safe' enough to leave, it's too late, and I end up having to cancel. I feel so awful about it. 

I hope I don't sound like a terrible friend or employee. I really am trying my hardest to keep up with everything. Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things in a specific order if you were absolutely certain that everything was correct and there were no mistakes?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I guess... if I could somehow magically just *know* for absolute certain that there were no mistakes? Maybe I wouldn't have to. But the tricky part is, I just never feel certain. Even if I know logically I probably did it right, that awful feeling doesn't go away unless I do my routine. 

I know I keep bringing up the exact same examples—I'm so sorry, I really must sound incredibly boring and repetitive today! But it's just that, to calm myself down, I have to go through that whole process. I end up reopening the spreadsheets, rereading the emails line by line, checking the locks and those payment confirmations over and over in that set order... it's the only way I can finally get to that 'safe' feeling. 

So even if someone promised me everything was perfectly correct, I think I'd still be stuck at my desk hours later, doing all of that, ending up with nothing actually finished... just trying to find that feeling of certainty for myself. 

I hope I'm not sounding too unreasonable or silly when I say that. Did that actually answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how it works in my head.
Do you feel like the specific order of your checks has to be symmetrical or follow a specific pattern to feel complete?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's necessarily about symmetry, like things having to be perfectly even on both sides or anything like that. It's more about... a pattern, I guess? Or just a very specific routine. 

I know I keep saying this, and I'm so sorry for repeating myself again, but it's like I was mentioning before... to calm myself down, I just have to go through that exact sequence. I end up reopening the spreadsheets, then rereading the emails line by line, then checking the locks, and then the payment confirmations. It has to be in that set order, over and over, until it finally feels 'safe.' 

If I skip a step or do it out of order, the pattern is broken, and I just have to start all over again. That's why some nights I'm still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished. I just... I have to complete the pattern perfectly. 

I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound like I'm just obsessing over silly little details, but that pattern is the only thing that works. Am I explaining that okay for you?
Do you feel like your checking behaviors help you regain a sense of control when you're feeling overwhelmed or anxious?

Um, yes... I suppose that's exactly what it is. It's like I'm just trying to get a handle on things when I feel that awful anxiety bubbling up. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm trying to be difficult or controlling, I just... I get so overwhelmed.

And, well, I know I've brought this up a few times already—I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the best examples. But when I get that anxious feeling, to calm myself down, I just have to go through my little routine. Reopening the spreadsheets, rereading the emails line by line, checking the locks, and then the payment confirmations... over and over in that set order until it finally feels 'safe.' 

It does give me a sense of control, I guess, even though it means some nights I’m still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished. It's just my way of trying to manage the stress so I don't let anyone down. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I really want to be helpful.
Do you think your checking behaviors are more about avoiding mistakes or achieving perfection?

Oh, um... wow, that's a really thoughtful question. I'm actually not entirely sure? I hope it's okay that I don't have a definitive answer for you on that one. 

I suppose... well, working with numbers and data all day, you really don't want to be the person who messes up. So maybe it starts as just wanting to avoid making a mistake? I really don't want to sound like I'm some sort of demanding perfectionist, because I know that can come across as rigid or difficult, and I promise I'm really not trying to be like that at all. I just want to do a good job and not cause any trouble for my team. 

But honestly, I haven't really thought about the difference between the two before. I'm so sorry if I'm rambling and not giving you a very straight answer. Does that make any sense at all? Or... is there one that you think fits better based on what I've been telling you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors would be less compelling if the tasks you were checking didn't have to be done in a precise manner?

Um, oh... that's an interesting way to look at it. I guess if the tasks didn't have to be so precise, maybe I wouldn't feel quite so... compelled? 

I really don't know for sure, though. I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a better answer. It's just that my job—working with data and all those numbers—it kind of demands a certain level of precision, you know? So I haven't really had the chance to see what I'd do if it didn't matter as much. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or trying to avoid the question. I really am trying my best to think about it.

Do you think that makes a difference? I mean, if I was doing something less... exact, do you think I wouldn't need to do my little routine as much? I'm sorry, I don't mean to turn the question around on you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things repeatedly if you knew that making a small mistake would have no significant consequences?

Oh, um... if there were no consequences at all? That's... well, that's a lovely thought, honestly. I'd like to think I wouldn't need to do it as much. I really would. 

But... well, I know I've mentioned this before, and I'm so sorry to keep bringing up the same examples, I just want to make sure I'm painting the right picture for you. Even if someone told me a mistake wouldn't matter, I think I'd still get that awful, nagging feeling. And to calm myself down, I'd probably still end up doing the same things... reopening the spreadsheets, rereading the emails line by line, checking the locks, and the payment confirmations. I just have to do them over and over in that set order until it finally feels 'safe.' 

I really try not to let it get out of hand, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just wasting time on purpose. But even if the mistake didn't matter, my brain just won't let it go until the routine is done, and... well, like I said, some nights I'm still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished. 

I'm sorry, does that make me sound completely unreasonable? I hope you understand I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you can help me. Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Do you feel like the order of your checking actions has to follow a specific rule or sequence to feel complete?

Oh, um... yes, actually. I hope it doesn't sound too strange, but... yes, it does feel like it has to be in a certain order. I know I mentioned earlier about the spreadsheets and the emails and everything... I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly. 

When I get that terrible feeling, I can't just check things randomly. I have to do it exactly the same way every time. First I reopen the spreadsheets, then I reread the emails line by line, then I check the locks, and finally the payment confirmations. And I have to do it over and over in that exact set order. If I mess up the sequence or get interrupted, I feel like I have to start all over again, or else it just doesn't feel 'safe.' 

I really try to be efficient about it, I promise. I don't want to be a bother or slow things down at work. But... well, because I have to do it in that specific sequence until it feels right, that's why I sometimes end up at my desk for hours without actually finishing anything new. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terribly rigid and silly for a grown woman to be doing. I really hope you don't think less of me for it. Does that answer your question about the sequence? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are more about regaining a sense of control over your work and life or about avoiding the fear of making a mistake?

Oh, um... that's a really deep question. I'm not sure I've ever thought about it quite like that before. 

I guess... well, I don't really know if it's about control or just being afraid of messing up. I mean, nobody likes making mistakes, especially not with data, right? I always just want to do a good job and make sure everything is perfectly correct. I don't want to cause any trouble for anyone else. 

I suppose... maybe it's a little bit of both? But I honestly couldn't say for sure which one is the main reason. I'm sorry, I wish I had a clearer answer for you. I feel like I should know myself better than that, especially at my age. 

Do you think it's usually one or the other for people who do this sort of thing? I hope it's okay that I don't have a definitive answer for you. I just want to make sure I'm not misleading you by guessing. Is it alright if I just say I'm not entirely sure?
Do you think your checking behaviors are primarily driven by a fear of making mistakes or by a desire to achieve perfection in your work and daily tasks?

Oh, goodness... um, that feels a lot like what you just asked, and I feel just awful that I'm still so unsure. I'm sorry to be so unhelpful with these deeper questions. 

I suppose... well, working with numbers and data all day, making a mistake and not being perfect kind of feel like the exact same thing to me. I just really want to be diligent and do a good job, you know? I don't want to let my team down or have anyone think I'm careless. So maybe... maybe I try to be perfect just so I don't make a mistake? 

Oh dear, I'm just talking in circles now, aren't I? I'm so sorry. I really wish I could give you a simple 'this one or that one' answer, but it all just feels sort of... tangled up together in my head. I hope you're not getting frustrated with me. Is it okay that I can't quite pull those two things apart? I just really want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Do you feel like the order of your checks has to be symmetrical or have a specific rhythm to it?

Oh, um... symmetrical? Or a rhythm? I... I don't think so. I'm sorry, I hope I'm understanding you correctly. 

I don't really notice a beat to it or anything like that. It's just... that specific order I mentioned before. The spreadsheets, the emails, the locks, the payments. It's not about making it look balanced or sound musical, I don't think. It's just... the way it has to be done to feel right. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm giving you a lot of 'no's and 'I don't know's today. I really hope I'm not being a difficult patient. I just want to be as honest as I can so you have the right information. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things repeatedly if you had someone you trusted double-checking your work?

Oh, wow. Um... that's an interesting thought. I've actually never had anyone double-check my work like that, since I usually handle the data on my own. 

I guess... I would like to think that having someone I trust look it over would help? It sounds really nice in theory. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I really want to be honest with you... I think I'd probably still check it anyway. Even if they were wonderful and thorough. 

I'd probably just worry that they missed something, or that I gave them the wrong file to check in the first place, and then it would still be my fault. So I'd probably end up checking their checking, if that makes any sense? 

Oh, I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible or controlling. I really do trust my coworkers, I promise! It's just... the feeling doesn't really go away until I see it with my own eyes. Is that... is that a bad thing to admit? I hope you don't think less of me for saying that. I just want to give you the most accurate picture I can.
